in_hebrew.name: רוֹכֶל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: רוֹכֶל, (Rochel), ​מְקוֹר־קְבוּדָה, ​מְקוֹר־עֲבוּדָה, ​(מְקוֹר, ​'origin', ​'well', ​'fountain', ​'head'; ​q​​b​d, ​'acquired', ​'obtained'; ​​​​​​a​​​, ​'service', ​'labour', ​'work')​. ​ ​in Hebrew, the name Rochel is derived from the Hebrew words for 'fountain' or 'well' (​'mְקוֹר'), and 'acquired' or 'obtained' (​'q​​d), signifying a place of spiritual refreshment or a wellspring of life. ​in the Christian tradition, the name Rochel is associated with the biblical figure of Rachel, the wife of Jacob, who represents the ideal of a devoted wife and mother. ​The name Rochel is also linked to the concept of spiritual service or labour, highlighting the importance of selfless devotion to one's faith and community.

in_greek.name: Αυγγελλη
in_greek.long_meaning: Αυγγελλη, (Aggelλη), Περόπολεωσ, τελλό, πτελλό, περόπολεωσ, Δομειποτιγεωσ. ​ ​in Greek, the name Aggelλη is derived from the words for 'messenger' (Τυλλό), 'angel' (πτελλό), and 'messenger of God' (περότ϶υς). ​in the Christian tradition, the name Aggelλη is associated with the divine messengers who appear in the Bible, such as the angel Gabriel, who announced the birth of Jesus. ​The name Aggelλη is also linked to the concept of spiritual guidance and protection, highlighting the importance of divine intervention in human life.

in_latin.name: Rochella
in_latin.long_meaning: Rochella, (Fons laborum, fons meritorum), ​Well of toil, well of merit. ​in Latin, the name Rochella is derived from the words for 'well' or 'spring' (fons), and 'toil' or 'merit' (laborum, meritorum). ​in the Christian tradition, the name Rochella is associated with the concept of spiritual labor or merit, highlighting the importance of selfless devotion to one's faith and community. ​The name Rochella is also linked to the idea of a wellspring of life, representing a source of spiritual refreshment and guidance.
